cause_of_death: V2 DETA-NONOate repair FAILED. NO release starts at 48.6 pmol/cm²/s but decays below 1.0 threshold after 4.7 days (20h half-life too short for 30-day sustained release). Frozen criterion required sustained >= 1.0 for 30 days. Article XXXVI §4: repair budget = 1, second failure terminal.

reusable_negative_knowledge.headline: Chemical NO donors with <24h half-life cannot sustain 30-day anti-biofilm NO release from a fixed-loading catheter polymer.
reusable_negative_knowledge.V1_failure: Enzymatic NO secretion (eNOS + L-arginine) fails due to substrate depletion in CSF (L-arginine ~10-20 µM, too low).
reusable_negative_knowledge.V2_failure: DETA-NONOate (20h half-life) decays below therapeutic threshold after 4.7 days. Exponential release kinetics mean 95% of NO is released in first 4.5 half-lives (~3.75 days).
reusable_negative_knowledge.implication: Any NO-based anti-biofilm mechanism for chronic implantable shunts needs either: (a) NO donor with >7-day half-life (e.g., SNAP, published half-life ~weeks), (b) refillable NO donor reservoir, or (c) catalytic NO generation from CSF constituents (not L-arginine dependent).
reusable_negative_knowledge.toxicity_note: Total NO release (5.05 µmol/cm²) was within toxicity limit (10 µmol/cm²). Toxicity is not the constraint; sustained release is.

history.V2_R313: DETA-NONOate, 48.6→0.0 over 30 days, 4.7/30 days above threshold
